LexAI is built with Gemini 2.5 Flash · Vercel Serverless · React 18 (CDN) · Node.js. Most people sign contracts they don't fully understand. Not because they're careless. [3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: FinSight
A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q. FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[2] Project: Silhouette
Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. [3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. [3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: AI Neighborhood Watch
AI Neighborhood Watch is built with Flask · PostgreSQL · Gemini · ElevenLabs · Leaflet.js · Tailwind · pydub. Safety information in most neighborhoods lives in three different Facebook groups, a NextDoor thread, and someone's memory. There's no map. No categories. No way to just know what's been happening nearby. I built the map. Residents drop incidents on a Leaflet layer, Gemini auto-categorizes them, and everything renders as color-coded markers in real time. But the part I'm most proud of is the daily briefing: two AI voices, Ava and Mateo, get a script generated each morning, ElevenLabs synthesizes them separately, and pydub stitches them into a broadcast-ready MP3. A neighborhood safety podcast, generated overnight, every night, automatically.

A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. [3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. [3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[6] Project: FinSight
The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[1] Project: FinSight
A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q. FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. [3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[5] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. [3] Project: AI Neighborhood Watch
AI Neighborhood Watch is built with Flask · PostgreSQL · Gemini · ElevenLabs · Leaflet.js · Tailwind · pydub. Safety information in most neighborhoods lives in three different Facebook groups, a NextDoor thread, and someone's memory. There's no map. No categories. No way to just know what's been happening nearby. I built the map. Residents drop incidents on a Leaflet layer, Gemini auto-categorizes them, and everything renders as color-coded markers in real time. But the part I'm most proud of is the daily briefing: two AI voices, Ava and Mateo, get a script generated each morning, ElevenLabs synthesizes them separately, and pydub stitches them into a broadcast-ready MP3. A neighborhood safety podcast, generated overnight, every night, automatically.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[5] Project: Silhouette
Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Smart Doc Finder
Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. Smart Doc Finder watches your document directory in real time via Redis Streams, chunks anything large into contextual blocks, embeds every chunk into Redis Vector Search, and checks a semantic cache before it even runs a query, so if someone asked something similar recently, it returns instantly. One Redis instance. Three jobs: event streaming, vector database, semantic cache. The architecture was the puzzle. Natural language search that actually works was the point.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

Question: What else should I know about Silhouette?

Smart Doc Finder is built with Python · Redis (Streams + Vector DB + Semantic Cache) · MongoDB · React · Docker. Keyword search has one fatal flaw: you have to remember exactly how something was worded to find it. That's not how memory works, and it's not how understanding works either. PostHog Engineering Impact Dashboard is built with Python · Airflow · dbt · PostgreSQL · FastAPI · Redis · React · Vercel. Engineering teams generate a lot of data and almost no insight. Commits, PRs, reviews, issues: all happening, none of it connected. I wanted to know: what does a fair, comparable measure of engineering output actually look like? So I built the whole pipeline. The interesting part wasn't the stack. It was deciding what to measure and why.

[3] Project: FinSight
FinSight is built with Python · Mistral-7B · QLoRA (PEFT, bitsandbytes) · Transformers · vLLM · FastAPI · SEC EDGAR + XBRL. A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

[3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. A first adapter is trained. The comparison against base Mistral, base Mistral with retrieved examples, and a large hosted model, on accuracy, cost per release and latency, is the next result, and its numbers go here once it has run. [3] Project: Silhouette
Silhouette is built with Python · OR-Tools CP-SAT · YAML rules engine · CIEDE2000 colour · JavaScript · Mask2Former (W1). A styling reasoning engine built on a solver that picks the outfit and explicit rules that explain why it works. Most wardrobe apps match garments by how they look. Silhouette is a styling reasoning engine: a solver assembles outfits against explicit styling rules and explains, with numbers, why each one works on a given frame. A language model never picks the outfit. The core measurement is lift: how much longer the leg line reads than it really is, based on where the outfit puts the visual break. Eighteen rules, written as YAML, score proportion, volume balance and CIEDE2000 colour contrast at the break. An exact solver checks every candidate outfit (158 µs each), a CP-SAT planner picks a week of outfits from one shared wardrobe, and every line of explanation comes from a rule that fired, not from generated text. The rule weights were set by hand, so I built an eval harness to fit them: a sampler that aims for rule coverage, Spearman and weighted kappa, and a fitter that only writes new weights when they beat the hand-set ones on held-out outfits. Against a synthetic rater it moved both planted weights the right way. Next are real expert labels (none yet) and garment segmentation, a Mask2Former model on Fashionpedia that is written but not yet trained.

A Mistral-7B model trained to read an earnings press release and return its key figures as JSON. When a company reports a quarter, the four numbers a trading desk wants first (revenue, net income, diluted EPS and the period end) sit in a press release next to year-ago and year-to-date figures that look almost the same. FinSight fine-tunes Mistral-7B-Instruct with QLoRA to read an earnings release and return those four fields as JSON. The labels come free from the SEC. I pull each release (8-K Exhibit 99.1) from EDGAR, label it with the figures the company later filed in XBRL, and keep it only when those exact figures appear in the text the model reads. Train, validation and test are split by company, so the test set is made of companies the model never saw. Training runs in 4-bit on a free 16 GB T4. A first adapter is trained. The repo also has vLLM serving behind a FastAPI endpoint, a CI eval gate, and a live watcher that answers new releases as they are filed and scores itself weeks later against the 10-Q.
